summary: A 1964 Forest Service steel tower on Los Pinos Mountain in San Diego County, replacing a 1925 wooden tower; described as staffed. A directory marks it Gone; unresolved.

facts.design: Live-in cab on a 30 ft steel tower. NHLR: 14 x 14 ft CL-100 cab; FFLA San Diego-Riverside chapter: 13 x 13 ft CL-30 series cab
facts.status_note: NHLR and the FFLA chapter describe the 1964 tower as a current Forest Service lookout; Peakbagging.com says it is staffed most of the year. A firelookout.org directory list marks a Los Pinos Mountain entry Gone; not resolved.

staffing.status: staffed by Forest Service employees (FFLA chapter); Peakbagging.com says staffed most of the year

access.note: Described as an active Forest Service lookout. The FFLA chapter says the road to the lookout is paved; no source says visitors may climb the tower.

visit.trail_note: FFLA San Diego-Riverside chapter says the road to the lookout is paved and the tower has electric service, running water, a telephone and a shower in a service building at ground level.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes a 14 x 14 ft CL-100 live-in cab; the FFLA San Diego-Riverside chapter describes a 13 x 13 ft CL-30 series steel cab. Both put the cab on a 30 ft steel tower. Not resolved; the story reports both.

The firelookout.org directory list marks a Los Pinos Mountain entry Gone, while NHLR, the FFLA chapter and Peakbagging.com describe a current, staffed Forest Service lookout. The Gone label may refer to the 1925 wooden tower, but no source says so. The story treats the tower as current and staffed and states the conflict.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record says this entry shares a register number with another lookout; I did not identify the other entry, and NHLR gives US 742, CA 81 for this one. The FFLA San Diego-Riverside page says the staffed tower is the only one on the Cleveland National Forest still staffed by Forest Service employees; that is a claim by the chapter, not a Forest Service source. The socalfirelookouts.org page in the brief could not be reached (DNS failure). AllTrails returned HTTP 403. The Facebook ALERTCalifornia snippet (1925 original, 1964 replacement) was not opened. Public climbing rules and current staffing are unverified.
